Contract status

FHT contract status
StatusReleased contract. schemaVersion "1.0" shipped in shared specification v0.7.0 on 2026-11-20.
Versions this schema accepts1.0. A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state any earlier minor of the same major, and holds each of them to that minor: what a later minor allows is invalid in an earlier one.
What it describesFHT is the released FAIR-bioHeaders 1.0 header contract for reference transcriptome FASTA, published in shared v0.7.0. It records construction history, supplied sample/library context, provenance and reported measurements.
What it does not coverA header describes the transcriptome file, not per-record expression, gene-model structure, biological correctness or repository acceptance.

Serializations with verified support

  • Published synthetic JSON/FASTA/typed-HTML triples cover the three construction values and mixed molecules. Typed HTML uses the schema identity as its F1 itemtype; JSON-LD is unsupported.
  • YAML preserves extension data; HTML omits extension fields under M5 and reports the omission.

Tools that implement this contract

  • Published fair-bioheaders 0.13.1 supports normal released FHT without a development gate. The actual noneditable published wheel validated all 14 browser HTML/YAML exports from the seven published source records and converted them to equal typed JSON.
  • The browser builder uses the exact published schema, C1 arithmetic and explicit safe-number limits. File-byte, parent and biology checks remain separate; website deployment requires its own live receipt.
  • Owning development remains in FHT-Specification; the shared specification is the publication authority.

Schema location

  • Fixed schema URL of the current release: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/v0.7.0/fht.json. Cite the release a record targets: never hard-code a "latest" schema, and never check an unknown version against a different one.
  • The same bytes at the release tag: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/v0.7.0/fht.json, also fixed at commit 623c79fe58.
  • Logical schema identity ($id), alias registration pending: https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fht/v0.7.0. Use the raw-tag resource above for published bytes.
  • Schema-version registry: schemas/versions.json and docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md.

Field reference

Every field of the contract appears here, including the fields and objects inherited from the shared core: nothing is left out because another type also uses it. Required means the key must be present; when present, requires lists the members that become mandatory once you supply an optional object. Constraints are reproduced verbatim from the schema, so a pattern you see here is the pattern the validator matches. Examples are the values stated by the released example records, which are synthetic, or an illustrative value where no example reaches the field.

Top-level fields

Every field of the published FHT 1.0 record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, apart from the x- extension fields listed last. Nine fields are required: schema, schemaVersion, transcriptome, assemblyType, taxon, version, metadataAuthor, dateCreated and checksum.

assemblyTypeRequiredstring
  • one of: de novo | genome-guided | annotation-derived

Construction case for the whole described transcript set

de novo: reads reconstructed with no reference genome constructing or grouping the assembly; genome-guided: read evidence plus a reference constructed models or grouped reads; annotation-derived: sequences extracted from existing annotation coordinates and the matching genome.

It describes construction, not quality or deposit class. There is deliberately no mixed or unknown value: a composite or uncertain history leaves the record incomplete until it is reviewed.

Genome guidance alone never justifies a transcribedFrom parent link.

annotation-derivedPublished v0.7.0 synthetic FHT example: annotation-derived.fht source
checksumRequiredstring
  • pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=$
  • length: exactly 44

Exact-file SHA-512/256 checksum under the shared exclusion rules

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Units: standard padded base64 of the SHA-512/256 digest

Shared rules R1–R4 cover exact FASTA bytes excluding the root checksum line, using canonical padded base64 of SHA-512/256. A structural checksum check is not byte verification.

Published fair-bioheaders 0.13.1 bundles this released FHT contract. Metadata validation alone does not recompute file bytes; use the released file-verification commands with the actual files.

Legacy MD5 values and T/U conversion are not header repairs.

completenessOptionalobject (Completeness)when present, requires lineageDataset, completeSingle, completeDuplicated, fragmented, missing, totalmembers listed belownone stated

Optional BUSCO completeness counts from the actual run. lineageDataset must match the pinned shared pattern (a name ending in _odb plus one or more dot-separated numeric version components, such as hymenoptera_odb10 or hymenoptera_odb12.2), as widened by shared #170 for v0.6.0. Do not rename or coerce a measured lineage to fit the pattern; if a measured value cannot be represented, omit completeness and keep the lineage and counts in documentation. When completeSingle, completeDuplicated, fragmented, missing and total are all supplied as integers, the four mutually exclusive component counts must sum exactly to total (C1). This cross-field arithmetic is checked by the owning reader, not expressible in standard JSON Schema.

Counts from an actual BUSCO run only; a legacy free-text completeness string is never converted into counts. Counts describe ortholog groups, not transcripts or genes.

The lineage pattern accepts _odb plus one or more dot-separated numeric version components, so hymenoptera_odb12.2 is representable: shared FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#170 widened it for v0.6.0 and FHT-Specification#34 mirrored the widened grammar into the development model. Do not rename or coerce a measured lineage to fit the pattern; if a measured value cannot be represented, omit completeness and keep the lineage and counts in documentation.

derivedFromOptionalarray of DerivedFrom objectsarray of DerivedFrom objects, 1 or morewhen present, requires headerType, checksum, relationshipmembers listed belownone stated

Reviewed FAIR-bioHeaders parent-file relationships only. This contract permits an FHT filteredFrom parent or an FHR transcribedFrom parent when the transcript bases were extracted from that genome; genome guidance alone never justifies transcribedFrom. Annotation coordinates and other sources stay in relatedLink/documentation until the shared relationship vocabulary is decided (#54). A genome-guided set whose final sequences were actually extracted from that genome also uses FHR transcribedFrom; construction history alone does not establish the source of its bases. The shared DerivedFrom object requires the parent's FHR-family checksum; an accession alone is not a verified family link. Identical parent entries are not allowed. A parent checksum uses canonical padded base64 for the 32-byte SHA-512/256 digest.

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Permitted parent pairs are FHT+filteredFrom and FHR+transcribedFrom. Genome guidance alone does not establish extraction of transcript bases from a genome.

Each parent needs its canonical SHA-512/256 checksum. The array is non-empty and identical parent entries are rejected; supplied accessions and SeqCol digests do not replace exact file identity.

A schema-valid assertion or matching parent checksum does not prove biological derivation.

strandednessOptionalstring
  • one of: unstranded | forward | reverse

Supplied library strandedness under the FHT read/read-1 convention: forward means the single read or read 1 is sense relative to the originating transcript, reverse means antisense. Unknown or mixed protocols are omitted, never defaulted to unstranded.

FHT's own normalization — unstranded, forward or reverse — where forward means the single read or read 1 is sense relative to the originating transcript.

It is not an ENA enum, not genomic plus/minus orientation, and not the orientation of exported transcript sequences. Unknown or mixed protocols are omitted, never defaulted to unstranded.

sample[] — supplied biological sample context

One entry per biological source. Pooled material is repeated entries, each with only the values actually known for that source.

  • The object is closed: an unknown key inside it is invalid, and so is an x- extension key at this level (rule R15).
  • One member must be supplied: tissue, tissueIdentifier, developmentalStage, condition, strain.
  • At least one member must be present in every entry; sample: [{}] is invalid.

Rules beyond a single field

FHT conditional and object-level rules, read from the schema bytes.
RuleWhat the contract requires
No key may contain a line feedpropertyNames rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.
The record is a closed objectadditionalProperties: false — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way. Legacy draft keys that were dropped (masking, license, the free-text completeness string) are therefore rejected, not tolerated.
Extension fields (rule R15)FHT 1.0 accepts top-level keys matching the published x- pattern under R15. There is no earlier released FHT minor to protect; every other unknown key is rejected.

What the schema cannot say

The contract is more than its JSON Schema. These requirements are normative for a conforming record, and a validator that cannot check them must say so:

  • The schema enforces requiredness, lexical constraints and permitted parent relationships. C1 and canonical checksum policy are additional runtime checks.
  • Structural validity does not verify sequence bytes, exact parent files or biological derivation. Counts are producer-reported, not a quality verdict.
  • Legacy fht-v0.1, the owning draft and the retired converter remain historical review inputs. Their citations, MD5 checksums and removed keys are not silently migrated.

It documents 67 fields: 30 at the top level and 37 inside 10 nested or reused objects. The published file also defines Author, Source, which no field of the record reaches. Regenerate and compare with python3 scripts/schema_fields.py --check, which the site checks run on every pull request. The specification repository stays the authority: this page is a rendering of it, not a second definition.
